paper_metadata.title: Extracting a function encoded in amplitudes of a quantum state by tensor network and orthogonal function expansion

summary: This paper proposes a gate-based quantum circuit method for reading out a function encoded in amplitudes by combining orthogonal-function expansion with an MPS ansatz. In the numerical study, a five-asset worst-of put option under the Black–Scholes model was approximated with D = r = 16 and niter = 5, reducing degrees of freedom from 1,048,576 cosine coefficients to 12,544 MPS parameters while achieving max errors of about 0.5086 versus Monte Carlo on random points and about 0.3164 versus the full cosine expansion.

experiments.description: Numerical experiment approximating a five-asset worst-of put option price using an MPS-based tensor-network quantum circuit, with classical preprocessing of orthogonal-function coefficients and classical simulation of the circuit optimization.

algorithm.variant: tensor-network-based quantum circuit for function readout / state-encoding optimization
algorithm.ansatz: matrix product state (MPS) circuit encoding orthogonal-function coefficients
algorithm.optimizer: alternating optimization via SVD update (no standard classical optimizer named)

hyperparameters.grid_points: ngr = D in the classical numerical experiment

algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial values of the unitaries V1,...,Vd-1 chosen randomly

problem_formulation.encoding_details: function values on a d-dimensional grid are amplitude-encoded in |f>; orthogonal-function coefficients are encoded via an MPS circuit
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize fidelity F = <f|f~> between the target function state and the generated approximation state
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: none reported beyond right-canonical MPS constraints and SVD-based unitary updates

problem_instance.description: Five-asset worst-of put option pricing under the Black–Scholes model; target function is the option price V(0,s) over asset prices s

dataset_specification.preprocessing: option values on grid points computed by Monte Carlo integration with 10^5 sample paths; 10^4 random sample points drawn from the BS model at t=1 with initial value (K,...,K)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: grid-point values of f(s) computed by Monte Carlo integration; cosine basis used on equally spaced grid points; lower bound Li = 0.01K and upper bound Ui set by Eq. (C6)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: accuracy evaluated on the diagonal line s1=...=sd and on 10^4 random sample points; compared against Monte Carlo values and full cosine expansion

implementation_details.classical_solver: ITensor library; Monte Carlo integration via TF Quant Finance
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: compute orthogonal-function coefficients a_l by Eq. (7) from grid values; in the numerical experiment, the oracle V_OF is absorbed into preprocessing
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: read out MPS parameters from optimized unitaries and multiply by normalization factor C to form C f~

speedup_claims.factor: parameter reduction from 1048576 to 12544 coefficients (about 83.6x fewer parameters)
speedup_claims.conditions: for the five-asset worst-of put option numerical experiment with D = r = 16
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a reduction in degrees of freedom / model size, not a proven runtime speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: O(d r^2 D + r D^2) vs O(D^d)
speedup_claims.conditions: for evaluating the MPS-based approximation versus a general d-dimensional tensor of coefficients
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an algorithmic complexity claim for function evaluation, not an experimentally measured speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly quantified; circuit-based function readout and MPS optimization discussed qualitatively
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(d r^2 D + r D^2) for evaluating the MPS-based approximation; naive full expansion is O(D^d)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A future fault-tolerant or NISQ gate-based implementation would need the oracle O_f, the orthogonal-function state-preparation oracles V_OF^i, and repeated Hadamard-test-based estimation of O(M^2) Pauli coefficients per MPS update; the paper does not provide a hardware resource estimate.
limiting_factors: No experimental quantum hardware run is reported
No demonstrated end-to-end runtime advantage over classical methods
Classical preprocessing is substantial in the numerical experiment
The paper explicitly states that query complexity and convergence guarantees are left for future work
The method is an approximation/readout procedure rather than a benchmarked quantum speedup

notes: No actual gate count / qubit count / transpiled depth is reported for the numerical experiment; the paper states the experiment was performed on a classical computer using the ITensor library, so hardware.type is inferred as simulator_other/classical simulation rather than a real QPU.

The paper does not report a concrete qubit count for the numerical experiment because the quantum circuit is modified away in the classical simulation; the underlying algorithmic circuit would use dmdeg qubits for VMPS and dmgr qubits for VApp, but the experiment itself does not instantiate a hardware run.
The paper reports a classical numerical experiment and qualitative algorithmic complexity claims, but no empirical quantum advantage.
